methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops targeting underserved communities in Hampton Roads signal grassroots capability-building that could distribute AI fluency beyond metro hubs, directly addressing the technology gap through peer-to-peer learning models.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU's partnership with AI Ready RVA creates institutional infrastructure for distributed AI education and community impact, positioning Richmond as a second gravity well that could counterbalance NoVA's concentration if scaled effectively.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches WorkAI Lab to prepare leaders for new era of technology - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's WorkAI Lab represents capability-building in a non-metro region, testing whether smaller cities can develop deep AI leadership competencies without proximity to NoVA's infrastructure—a critical indicator for distribution potential.

signals.title: NoVa lawmakers take AI cash while residents resist data centers - opensecrets.org
signals.signal_reading: Local resistance to data centers despite lawmakers taking AI industry cash reveals a disconnect where NoVA hosts AI infrastructure without cultivating broad community buy-in or distributed benefits, risking shallow engagement even in the concentration zone.

signals.title: Virginia's AI boom quietly drained the entire regional electricity grid - Yahoo Finance
signals.signal_reading: NoVA's data center boom draining the regional electricity grid exemplifies how infrastructure concentration creates systemic dependencies that reinforce the metro-rural divide, making distributed AI development harder by monopolizing critical resources.
